summary: This Dockerfile creates a lightweight Python container for running a FastAPI web application. It starts with a slim Python image, installs the FastAPI framework, copies in the application code, and configures the container to run a Uvicorn web server on port 82 with hot-reload enabled so changes take effect immediately.

explanations.2: The `slim` variant is a smaller, stripped-down version of Python that includes only essential packages, saving disk space compared to the standard Python image.
explanations.5: WORKDIR sets the default directory inside the container where all subsequent commands will run — think of it like `cd /app` happening automatically when the container starts.
explanations.8: The `--no-cache-dir` flag tells pip not to store the downloaded packages locally in the image, which saves space since we won't need to reinstall them.
explanations.11: COPY takes a file from your computer (the left `main.py`) and places it into the container (the right `main.py`).
explanations.15: CMD specifies what command runs when the container starts; `--reload` watches for file changes and restarts the server automatically, and `--host 0.0.0.0` makes the server accessible from outside the container.
